assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, glucagon-like peptide processing and the active truncated peptide) led to a new therapeutic class that has transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care and shows benefit in cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The path from basic gut-hormone physiology to a major drug class is a clear, original and highly consequential Physiology or Medicine story.
assessment.attribution: Decisive academic contributions are Holst (GLP-1 secretion and physiology, incretin effect), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, intestinotrophic GLP-2, translational work) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form). Knudsen led the industrial development of liraglutide and semaglutide, but the three-laureate limit forces a choice and the proposed set is my judgment of the scientific discovery core, not a certainty.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, large randomized trials and wide clinical adoption; recognition is timely and arguably pressing given the societal impact.
uncertainties: Credit among Habener, Mojsov, Holst, Drucker and Knudsen is contested and Habener is not on the supplied credit list.
Whether the committee prefers to honour the discovery of the peptide's physiology or the drug development is unresolved; I rely on memory for the detailed priority history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened the field of engineered cell therapy. This is a clear conceptual and clinical breakthrough with broad impact on cancer immunotherapy.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed early costimulatory CAR designs, June led the first clinical successes in leukemia and CLL, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive T-cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials. Other names (Eshhar, Kuwana, Brenner, Mackall, Gross) are not on the supplied list so the supplied credit is a constrained representation, and the split between concept and clinic is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and over a decade of follow-up; long-term safety and solid-tumour efficacy remain limited, but the hematologic efficacy is firmly established.
uncertainties: Attribution of the original CAR concept versus clinical translation is unresolved and some key contributors are absent from the credited names.
Late toxicities, including secondary T-cell malignancies, and limited activity in solid tumours qualify the final assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) turned spinal muscular atrophy, previously the leading genetic killer of infants, into a treatable disease. It is a rigorous mechanism-to-therapy story with a clear definition of the molecular target and as a neurologist I regard the clinical transformation as exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and the ISS-N1 target in the SMN2 context, and Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development at Ionis. The supplied credit is compact and fits a two-person prize; contributions by Gideon Dreyfuss, Judith Melki and Lefebvre for SMN1 gene discovery are not credited here, which is a limit of the list.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term clinical follow-up and independent confirmation across multiple antisense and gene therapy modalities; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Discovery of the SMN1 gene is a separate foundational contribution not captured in the credited names.
Antisense therapeutics may be considered a technology platform whose broader recognition might be better framed together with other RNA therapeutics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition established the proof of principle of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, converting chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease to a manageable one, and it triggered the kinase-inhibitor era of oncology.
assessment.attribution: Lydon initiated the programme and the chemistry and target concept, Druker drove the biological and clinical demonstration and Sawyers identified resistance mechanisms and extended the clinical paradigm. This is a fairly natural three-person configuration, though the role of Ciba-Geigy chemist Jürg Zimmermann is not credited.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of survival data, replication and widespread adoption; recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for medicinal chemistry (Zimmermann) and the earlier Rowley and Witte contributions on BCR-ABL are outside the credited list.
The Nobel committee historically has recognized the underlying cancer-gene discoveries and may regard the therapeutic step as distinct.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and elucidation of nutrient and growth signalling through TOR/mTOR is a fundamental discovery in cell growth control with consequences for metabolism, cancer, ageing, immunosuppression and neurobiology.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genes in yeast and defined the TOR pathway; Schreiber showed that the FKBP12-rapamycin complex inhibits the mammalian target. Sabatini also cloned mTOR contemporaneously and later made major contributions to nutrient sensing, but I have left him out, partly because the three-name limit and partly because of the unresolved credit and professional-conduct questions around him that I cannot verify.
assessment.maturity: Highly replicated over three decades; the clinical impact (rapalogs) is solid, though the broad human therapeutic effect beyond transplantation and some cancers is moderate.
uncertainties: Priority among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini, Brown and Sabatini's contemporaries (Abraham, Snyder) is unresolved.
I recall but have not verified the details of Sabatini-related controversies.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience a way to control defined cell populations with millisecond precision, transforming circuit-level causal analysis and enabling new approaches to disease models and potentially therapy (including vision restoration). The impact on basic research is very large and the idea is original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its neuronal deployment (Boyden, Deisseroth) are distinct steps, and Miesenböck provided earlier genetically targeted photostimulation. Six names exceed the three-laureate limit so the exclusion of Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck is a difficult trade-off.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for 15+ years; clinical translation is emerging (retinal optogenetics) but limited, so the prize would rest on the tool and its research impact.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit across six candidates is the central problem and any three-person configuration leaves out comparable contributors.
Therapeutic translation is early, so the case rests primarily on experimental utility.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like-particle vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other HPV-related cancers, a rare example of a prophylactic cancer-prevention vaccine with population-level effectiveness already visible as falling cervical lesion rates.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 virus-like particles with the NCI group and Frazer (with Jian Zhou) developed the L1/L2 VLP expression system; Zhou, who died in 1999, and the Georgetown/Rochester and Cambridge groups (Kirnbauer, Rose) are also part of the priority history and are not fully represented.
assessment.maturity: Strong real-world effectiveness data on cervical cancer incidence across countries; the long-term cancer outcomes are now emerging, so the case is mature.
uncertainties: Patent and priority disputes in VLP development are not fully resolved in my recollection and I have not verified them.
The 2008 prize already recognized HPV causation of cervical cancer, which may influence perceived novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identifying tau and alpha-synuclein as the principal components of pathological filaments in Alzheimer's disease, Lewy body disease and related conditions reframed neurodegeneration as proteinopathy and underpins biomarkers, seed-amplification assays and tau-targeted and synuclein-targeted therapeutic programmes.
assessment.attribution: Spillantini and Goedert identified alpha-synuclein in Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites and Goedert's group linked tau to the paired helical filaments of Alzheimer's disease; the pair is coherent. Earlier tau work (Kosik, Brion, Grundke-Iqbal) and the alpha-synuclein genetics (Polymeropoulos) are separate contributions.
assessment.maturity: Highly replicated and clinically influential, with cryo-EM filament structures and diagnostics validating it, though disease-modifying therapies are still unproven, which makes the translational completion premature.
uncertainties: The Alzheimer's side of the work relies on precedent contributions by others, and credit among tau discoverers is contested.
Therapeutic validation of the proteinopathy concept is still pending.
